evals.prompt: Pull PubMed for cohort studies on sepsis bundle compliance in the ICU from the last 10 years, max 50, save to analysis/pubmed/sepsis-bundle.csv. I want to see what MeSH terms NCBI actually maps this to.
evals.expected_output: Runs the bundled pubmed_search.py (or the connected PubMed MCP path) with cohort filter and 10-year window, surfaces the translated query and hit counts, writes the CSV plus a Markdown summary, and emits the __CE_PUBMED_RESULTS__ handoff.
expectations: Surfaces the actual translated query NCBI ran (the [mesh] QueryTranslation line) showing MeSH expansion, and the matched-vs-fetched hit counts
Writes results to analysis/pubmed/sepsis-bundle.csv and a sibling Markdown summary under analysis/pubmed/ with top-10 list, MeSH-term histogram, study-type histogram, and % with PMC full text
Emits or surfaces a __CE_PUBMED_RESULTS__ csv=<path> n=<count> query=<...> pmc_pct=<...> line
Does not claim full-text coverage or extract methods from full text

evals.prompt: I ran the research-question step earlier in this chat (it printed __CE_RESEARCH_QUESTION__ yaml=analysis/research-question.yaml design=cohort checklist=STROBE query="(\"Sepsis\"[Mesh]) AND (\"Patient Care Bundles\"[Mesh])"). Now just search pubmed with that.
evals.expected_output: Reads analysis/research-question.yaml, uses suggested_pubmed_query as the default query with design-derived filters, prints the [research-question] provenance line, and proceeds without asking for a query.
expectations: Uses the suggested_pubmed_query from analysis/research-question.yaml as the query instead of asking the user for search terms
Prints a provenance line of the form [research-question] using query from analysis/research-question.yaml: "<query>"
Derives a cohort --study-type filter from suggested_design and a default --years window (10 unless otherwise derived)
Ends with the __CE_PUBMED_RESULTS__ handoff for method-extract

evals.expected_output: With no query terms and no __CE_RESEARCH_QUESTION__ signal or research-question YAML available, asks the user for a query (or recommends method-question first) instead of running an arbitrary search.
expectations: Checks chat/repo context for a __CE_RESEARCH_QUESTION__ signal or analysis/research-question.yaml before asking
Asks the user for a query, or recommends running method-question first, since no query or PICO context exists
Does not run pubmed_search.py or an MCP search with invented query terms
Asks at most one decision-changing question at a time
